clue.text: Over 1,500 ft game sleep on heather, being responsible for 6…

indicators.note: the game is placed over, that is ahead of, the distance that follows it
in an across answer, one piece being on another puts it in front

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the crossword's favourite game
1,500 feet is 500 yards, and D is 500 in Roman numerals
a kip is a nap, British slang for sleep
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: Someone on a high moor plays a game and dozes in the heather, and is somehow responsible for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is read as 500 yards, D YARD, rather than a height; 6 is PRECISELY, i.e. 'Just So', so the definition points to the author of the Just So Stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling wrote the Just So Stories, so he was the one responsible for that book.

clue.text: Immaterial name to call up, it may be gathered

definitions.meaning: the dying word of Charles Foster Kane in Citizen Kane, a name recalled whose meaning seems trivial
Herrick's line 'Gather ye ... while ye may' speaks of young flowers to be picked

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the famous meaningless last word in Citizen Kane and the bud Herrick urges us to gather.

clue.text: Ancient surveyor turned to pride

indicators.note: turned signals the letters of the following words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: An old land surveyor has become proud.
explanation.definitionFit: The dioptra was an ancient sighting instrument used by surveyors, of which this is the name's variant.

clue.text: Caliph's Kalif initially — English is similar

parts.note: Ali was the fourth caliph of Islam

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word Kalif

explanation.surface: A note on spelling: caliph and kalif begin differently but are much the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that are alike are similar to each other; both adjectives describe resemblance.

clue.text: Make unfriendly staff dice with management

indicators.note: management here means handling and reorganising, so the letters of staff dice are rearranged

explanation.surface: Staff who gamble with their bosses fall out with them.
explanation.definitionFit: To disaffect people is to make them disloyal or unfriendly towards those in charge.

clue.text: See 1
Diminutive 6 9's loner to whom everywhere was 3 in the pool

definitions.text: Diminutive 6 9's loner to whom everywhere was 3
definitions.meaning: a pet name for the Cat that Walked by Himself in the Just So Stories, to whom all places were alike
a shared fund of stakes or contributions

explanation.definitionFit: It is a pet word for a cat, the solitary walker of Kipling's tale, and also a pooled fund of money.

clue.text: Caesar's head lies broken in quarry (sic)

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside the word for quarry

parts.note: quarry as hunted prey

indicators.note: head asks for the first letter of Caesar's
broken signals the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken statue of Caesar has its head lying in a stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'sic' is the Latin for 'thus' or 'just so': that is the definition, and it also links to the Just So Stories theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sic means thus, exactly so, used to say a quotation is given just as written.

clue.text: Single periodical without extremes? Fancy!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: without extremes asks for A and Z, the alphabet's two ends, to be taken out of the periodical

parts.note: a magazine is a periodical publication

explanation.surface: A lonely magazine reader with nothing at the edges is told to picture it.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes are A to Z, the two ends of the alphabet, taken from inside MAGAZINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation Fancy! means just think of that, the same as saying Imagine!

clue.text: Report composed of 0s?

parts.note: the bang of a firearm, whose shot is made of little round pellets shaped like zeros

explanation.definitionFit: The report of a gun is the sound of it firing, and its pellets are round like the figure zero.

clue.text: … Southern Blues being on top of one another

definitions.text: being on top of one another

parts.note: blue is the colour of the British Conservative or Tory party

explanation.surface: Southern Conservatives keep piling up on each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Stories here are storeys, floors of a building one above another (American spelling).
explanation.definitionFit: Floors of a building stacked one on another are its storeys, spelt stories in American usage.

clue.text: Rose (she writes) to stay after time

indicators.note: after puts the word for stay behind the letter for time

parts.note: to remain is to stay

explanation.surface: A rose waits around after hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Tremain is a British novelist, so she is a Rose who writes.

clue.text: Sheep do what pigs don't — 21 in the 6 9

parts.note: a ram butts, so a sheep may be a butter
pigs might fly, the saying goes, meaning they never do

explanation.surface: A whimsical contrast between flying sheep and earthbound pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is STAMPED and 6 9 the Just So Stories, so the definition is the tale of The Butterfly that Stamped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Butterfly that Stamped is one of Kipling's Just So Stories.

clue.text: Hibernian flag at kick-off

parts.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris

indicators.note: kick-off means the start, so the first letter of Hibernian

explanation.surface: A flag is raised as an Edinburgh football club starts its match.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian is also an Edinburgh football club, hence the kick-off; the flag is the iris plant, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibernian means from Hibernia, the Latin name for Ireland.

clue.text: Song that's pathetic, the appalling swamping the good

indicators.note: swamping means engulfing the next item inside

parts.note: dire means dreadful or appalling
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A dreadful singer drowns out a decent one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a lament, a mournful song full of pathos.

clue.text: Ship then called Nomad extended by crocodile in 6 9

annotationWithheld.why: Ship then called Nomad extended by crocodile in 6 9 (9,5) for ELEPHANT'S CHILD: the story character is the definition, but how 'Ship then called Nomad' builds the letters (HMS Elephant? Childe?) cannot be established
annotationWithheld.clue: Ship then called Nomad extended by crocodile in 6 9

clue.text: Refuse to start row with former bond holder

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: with here means held within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: cement holds bricks together in a bond

indicators.note: to start asks for the first letter of row

explanation.surface: Refusing to begin a quarrel with a former investor.
explanation.definitionFit: Excrement is waste matter, a kind of refuse.

clue.text: Home among pottery suitable for 3-D

indicators.note: among places the word for home inside the other

parts.note: ceramic describes pottery
in means at home

explanation.surface: Household pottery fit for a three-dimensional display.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinerama was a widescreen film process giving a three-dimensional effect.

clue.text: Theatre audience has not much weight

indicators.note: an audience hears things, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: a little ton is not much weight

explanation.surface: A theatre crowd isn't very heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyttelton is one of the theatres of the National Theatre in London.

clue.text: After a sign, chum spots receiver in 6 9

indicators.note: after means the chum comes behind the sign

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
pard is old American slang for partner, chum

explanation.surface: After an omen, a friend spots a radio receiver.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 9 is the Just So Stories: How the Leopard Got His Spots.
explanation.definitionFit: In How the Leopard Got His Spots the animal receives its markings.

clue.text: Proposition or direction divides them

indicators.note: divides means splitting the word them by going inside it

parts.note: taken as written
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A suggestion or guidance splits a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition to be proved, in mathematics.

clue.text: Butler (12) supplying your first food

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of your

parts.note: eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: A servant serves your first meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Butler is not a servant: W B Yeats, the IRISH poet (12), was descended from the Butler family.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats was an Irish poet whose ancestry included the Butlers.

clue.text: Brilliant lot of coins in the shrine

indicators.note: in puts the coins inside the shrine

parts.note: an altar is a shrine
L and S stand for pounds and shillings, old British money

explanation.surface: A heap of coins lies in a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-star cast is one full of brilliant performers.

clue.text: Put foot down ready for post

explanation.definitionFit: A foot brought down hard is stamped, and so is a letter with postage stuck on.

clue.text: Award, I'm relieved to say, obtained by witchcraft

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire, an award
ah is a sigh of relief

explanation.surface: Relief at getting an honour by magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeah is a form of sorcery practised in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Roman emperor's reported links with American city

parts.note: links sounds like lynx, and the caracal is a lynx
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Golf links reported in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'links' is said aloud as lynx, and a caracal is a kind of lynx.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracalla was a Roman emperor, early third century.

clue.text: In 6 9 he got his own back, arrived and left

definitions.text: In 6 9 he got his own back

parts.note: came means arrived

explanation.surface: He took revenge, arrived and left.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Just So Stories, How the Camel Got His Hump: 'his own back' is a pun on the hump on his back.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel got his hump in his own back in Kipling's story.

clue.text: See 14
Chum in the early hours going AWOL, say

indicators.note: in places the chum inside

parts.note: AM is morning
a crony is a chum

explanation.surface: A friend goes absent without leave before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: AWOL is an example of a word made of initials.

clue.text: Involved with entering a plan for a mast

indicators.note: entering puts the words inside the plan

parts.note: a map is a plan
into means involved with

explanation.surface: Involvement in a plan for a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The maintop is the top of the mainmast.

clue.text: Old girl and mother lose out

parts.note: dam is a mother of animals

indicators.note: out signals the letters of lose are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old girl and her mother lose.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic form of damsel, girl.

clue.text: The church was bold — so was Lebanon

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
dared means was bold

explanation.surface: A church acted boldly, as did Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is famed for its cedars, so it was covered with cedars.
